chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from the one who mentioned him, from Muhammad ibn Jahrash, who said:

Hakimah bint Musa narrated to me. She said: I saw al-Rida عليه السلام standing at the door of Bayt al-Hatab while he was conversing quietly, and I did not see anyone. So I said: O my master, to whom are you speaking secretly? He said: This is Amir al-Zahra'i; he came to me asking me and complaining to me. I said: O my master, I would love to hear his speech. He said to me: If you hear it, you will suffer fever for a year. I said: O my master, I would love to hear him. He said to me: Listen. So I listened, and I heard something like whistling, and fever overtook me, so I remained feverish for a year.

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Rida, the Imam mentioned in the report
key_terms.عَامِرٌ الزَّهْرَائِيُّ: the named being from the jinn who came to the Imam
key_terms.كَلَامَهُ: his speech or manner of speaking

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam al-Rida’s عليه السلام interaction with the jinn?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam al-Rida عليه السلام was addressed by a being unseen to Hakimah bint Musa, identified as Amir al-Zahra'i from the jinn. When she insisted on hearing his speech, she heard only a sound like whistling, and the Imam عليه السلام had warned her that doing so would cause her fever for a year, which then occurred. The report highlights the Imams' authority and interaction with the jinn regarding religious concerns.
